description: "A team of passionate software engineering students participating in our very first hackathon. Driven by curiosity and a desire to learn, we are here to tackle real-world space challenges, gain hands-on collaborative experience, and push our technical skills to the next frontier.
summary: SoftieCare is a native, offline-first Android app for astronaut health self-assessment on long-duration missions. The crew records 6 indicators (blood pressure, heart rate, glucose, body temperature, sleep and mood), and the app classifies each one as stable, not optimal or critical, links it to one of the 5 hazards of NASA's Human Research Program, and guides the crew through a countermeasure plan that ends with a new measurement. Because communication delays on deep-space missions make real-time telemedicine unreliable, the whole assessment runs on board with no network.
details:
SoftieCare shows the 6 indicators named in the challenge with their value, trend (last 7 readings) and level, plus an overall crew status. Each measurement follows a 3-step guided entry with animations and range validation. A single-attempt reaction test (PVT) can lower the behavioral state if reaction time is slow. When an indicator is in alert, the detail screen shows its linked HRP hazard, a trend chart and a countermeasure protocol; the guided plan ends with a wait time and a local notification that reminds the crew member to measure again. A demo simulator injects scenarios (nominal, radiation spike, isolation fatigue), and the crew can select the operating environment (transit to Mars, lunar base, pressurized rover).

Built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (Material 3), StateFlow for reactive state, Compose Canvas for charts and illustrations, AlarmManager and NotificationCompat for reminders, and Lottie for animations. Min SDK 26. No backend: 100% offline.

Limitations: values are entered manually, and classification thresholds are heuristic demo values, not clinical guidelines. Future work: sensor and wearable capture, environment-adjusted thresholds and a full clinical-length PVT.

AI use: Claude (Anthropic) assisted with brainstorming, research, code generation and debugging, documentation, and editing the demo video (trimming and English subtitles). All AI-assisted output was reviewed and integrated by the team.
